prompt: Let $G$ be a finite nonempty simple graph and $r$ a positive integer. Over valid merge sequences of $G$, minimise the maximum number of previous-partition parts reached from one original vertex by at most $r$ resolved pairs. Which graph parameter is defined?

answers.explanation: The radius is measured in the resolved-pair graph on original vertices. Optimising this local part count over merge sequences defines the parameter.
Clique-width counts construction labels. It corresponds in boundedness to radius-infinity merge-width, not a fixed finite radius.
Twin-width counts non-homogeneous neighbouring parts during binary contractions, rather than resolved-pair reachability.
Shrubdepth is a uniform height condition on coloured tree-models for a graph class.
Weak colouring numbers use an order on vertices and paths in the original graph, not merge sequences and resolved pairs.
Flip-width uses a pursuit game with adjacency flips; this is a decomposition-based definition.
Rank-width uses binary matrix ranks across cuts, not local balls of resolved pairs.

answers.text: The radius-$r$ width of one specified merge sequence.
answers.explanation: The minimum over all valid sequences is a graph parameter; a specified sequence has its own possibly larger width.
Neighbourhood complexity counts distinct neighbourhood traces, not parts encountered during a construction.
Component twin-width measures red components of contraction trigraphs, not bounded-radius reachability of original vertices.

sources.title: Dreier & Toruńczyk — Merge-width and First-Order Model Checking, Definitions 3.1–3.2 and §7 (June 2026 version)
